title: Check yourself: abstract classes or interfaces

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Which of these can an abstract class have that an interface cannot?

options.text: A method with a body that implementers inherit
options.says: Since Java 8 an interface can have default methods with a body, which implementing classes inherit.

options.text: A constructor that sets up instance fields
options.says: The page: abstract classes can have constructors and instance variables; interfaces have neither, only constants.

options.text: A static method that callers invoke by type name
options.says: Since Java 8 an interface can have static methods too.

questions.stem: Several unrelated classes must each promise a `draw()` method, and they share no code or state. What does this page recommend declaring for them?

options.text: An abstract class that lists the method
options.says: The page keeps abstract classes for a common base implementation shared by related classes, which these classes do not have.

options.text: A concrete class that lists the method
options.says: A concrete class carries an implementation, and the page recommends a contract without one for this case.

options.text: An interface that lists the method
options.says: The page: use interfaces when you want to define a contract for behaviour without implementation.

concepts: Abstract classes can have constructors and instance state, which interfaces cannot, while both may carry method bodies since Java 8.
Use an interface for a contract without implementation and an abstract class for a base implementation shared by related classes.
